title: Taiwan Arrival Checklist for Travelers & Digital Nomads (2026)

disclaimer.en: This guide is based on published requirements and the author's experience. Visa rules, fees, and procedures change. Verify current information with your nearest TECO (Taipei Economic and Cultural Office) and the Taiwan Tourism Bureau before making plans. This is not immigration or legal advice. LocalNomad is not a licensed immigration services organization (移民業務機構).
disclaimer.zh: 本指南依據已公布之規定及作者經驗撰寫。簽證規定、費用及程序可能隨時變更。請於出發前向最近之駐外館處（TECO）及交通部觀光署確認最新資訊。本內容不構成移民或法律諮詢建議。LocalNomad 並非經許可之移民業務機構。

phases.title: Before You Board
phases.description: Most of this can't be fixed at Taoyuan with jet lag and no data. Do it now.

items.label: Confirm your visa / entry type
items.description: Citizens of 65+ countries get 90-day visa-free entry. Staying longer? The DN Visa (Digital Nomad Visitor) covers up to 1 year but grants no ARC — similar to tourist for paperwork. The Gold Card is Taiwan's talent visa (ARC included); start 3–4 months early.
tips: Visa-free: bring return ticket proof in case immigration asks
Gold Card holders: your ARC is the card itself — active from approval date
DNV holders: no ARC issued — bank accounts and contract SIMs are not available
items.linkLabel: Taiwan Gold Card vs DN Visa: Which One?

items.label: Buy an eSIM before boarding
items.description: Klook, KKday, or Airalo all sell Taiwan eSIMs. Activate after landing. Skips the SIM counter queue at Taoyuan.
tips: Physical SIM counters (Chunghwa Telecom) exist in arrivals if you prefer a local SIM on arrival

items.label: Download essential apps
items.description: Four apps to install before you leave.
tips: LINE: Taiwan's universal messenger — landlord, coworkers, loyalty programs all on LINE
Google Maps: reliable for MRT routing in Taipei
Uber: often cheaper than hailing taxis, works from Taoyuan airport
Google Translate: camera mode reads Chinese menus and signs

items.label: Prepare documents folder (digital + printed)
items.description: Passport (6+ months validity), visa approval or return flight proof, health insurance documents, accommodation confirmation, 2 passport photos.
tips: Keep digital copies in cloud storage accessible offline

items.label: Withdraw or exchange NT$10,000–15,000 (~$310–470 USD)
items.description: Foreign credit cards work at most stores and restaurants, but night markets, small local shops, and some transit kiosks are cash-only.
tips: Exchange at the airport on arrival or withdraw from an ATM in the arrivals hall
Keep NT$500–1,000 in small bills specifically for night markets

phases.title: Day 0: Taoyuan Airport
phases.description: You just landed. Here's the sequence.

items.label: Clear immigration
items.description: Have your passport, visa documents (or return ticket for visa-free), and accommodation address ready. Usually 20–30 minutes even at peak times.

items.label: Confirm Gold Card / ARC is active
items.description: Gold Card = ARC (4-in-1). Pre-approved overseas means your ARC is active from Day 0 — you arrive with ARC in hand. Work permit holders receive a separate ARC after NIA registration. Checking this off unlocks banking and contract SIM steps.
tips: Gold Card holders: ARC is the card itself, activated from approval date
Work permit holders: ARC issued after NIA registration, typically 1–2 weeks

items.label: Get a SIM card or activate eSIM
items.description: Chunghwa Telecom counter in the arrivals hall. A 30-day unlimited 4G SIM runs NT$1,000–1,600 (~$31–50). Tourist/prepaid SIM requires passport only — no ARC needed.
tips: Get data before you leave the airport — you'll need it for navigation and Uber
Tourist/prepaid SIM: passport only. Contract SIM: requires ARC (resident only, unlocked later)

items.label: Buy an EasyCard (悠遊卡)
items.description: NT$500 package: NT$100 deposit + NT$400 loaded credit. Anonymous card — no ID required. Works on MRT, buses, YouBike, convenience stores, and vending machines.
tips: Available at the airport MRT station or any 7-Eleven
Top up at any convenience store register

items.label: Take Airport MRT to Taipei Main Station
items.description: NT$160, about 45 minutes. Trains run every 15 minutes, 6 AM–11 PM. Free WiFi on board. Use your EasyCard.
warnings: Arriving after 11 PM? Pre-book an airport shuttle or expect NT$1,200–1,500 for a taxi to central Taipei. Uber also works from Taoyuan.

phases.title: Days 1–7: Settle In
phases.description: Not everything needs to happen on day one. Spread it out.

items.label: Test your accommodation WiFi speed
items.description: Aim for 25+ Mbps for video calls. Most Taipei rentals exceed this easily.

items.label: Walk your neighborhood
items.description: Find the nearest MRT station, convenience store (7-Eleven or FamilyMart), pharmacy, and breakfast shop (早餐店 — cheap, fast, everywhere).

items.label: Hit a night market for dinner
items.description: Raohe, Ningxia, or Shilin are the big ones. Bring cash — night markets are cash-only. NT$500 covers a full meal plus snacks.
tips: Always cash-only at night markets — no card, no EasyCard
items.linkLabel: Taiwan Night Markets: A Foreigner's Guide

items.label: Set up LINE and add your accommodation host
items.description: LINE is Taiwan's universal messenger. Your landlord, coworkers, and local businesses all use it.

items.label: Add foreign credit card to Apple Pay or Google Pay
items.description: Accepted at most chain stores, restaurants, and convenience stores. Foreign Visa/Mastercard works almost everywhere except transit and night markets.
tips: LINE Pay registration is limited for foreigners without a local bank account — not a problem, your foreign card covers most things

items.label: Check power plug compatibility
items.description: Taiwan uses Type A/B plugs, same as the US. If you're coming from Europe, UK, or Australia, you need an adapter.
tips: Adapters available at any convenience store or electronics shop

phases.title: Week 1–4: Admin
phases.description: Resident visa holders only. Complete NIA registration within 30 days of arrival.

items.label: Register at NIA service center (移民署服務站)
items.description: Required for all resident visa holders (Gold Card, Work Permit). Bring ARC + passport + accommodation address. Must be done within 30 days of arrival — starts the NHI eligibility clock.
tips: Gold Card holders: register your Taiwan address within 30 days to start the NHI clock
Bring ARC, passport, and proof of address (lease agreement or accommodation letter)

items.label: Open a bank account
items.description: Cathay United and E.SUN Bank are foreigner-friendly. Requires ARC + passport + local phone number + personal chop or signature card.
tips: E.SUN has English-speaking staff at major branches
warnings: Bank accounts require ARC. DNV and visa-free visitors are not eligible.

items.label: Upgrade to a contract SIM (optional)
items.description: 2-year contract SIMs offer better rates and a stable local number. Requires ARC + passport.
tips: Tourist/prepaid SIMs work fine for most stays — only worth upgrading if settling long-term

phases.title: Month 1+: Long-term
phases.description: Resident visa holders: enroll in NHI and lock in long-term housing.

items.label: Enroll in NHI (全民健保, National Health Insurance)
items.description: Gold Card holders employed from Day 1 can enroll immediately. Unemployed Gold Card holders wait 6 months after NIA registration. During the wait, keep private travel insurance active.
tips: NHI clock starts from NIA registration date — not arrival date
6-month rule: max 1 departure under 30 days allowed, or the clock resets
Monthly premium: ~NT$749–1,000 for self-enrolled Gold Card holders
warnings: DNV and visa-free visitors are not eligible for NHI. Maintain private travel insurance.

items.label: Find long-term housing on 591.com.tw
items.description: Taiwan's main rental platform. Interface is in Chinese — use Google Translate camera mode to navigate.
tips: Landlords often prefer LINE for communication — set up your account first

items.label: Attend a meetup or coworking event
items.description: Kafnu, Impact Hub, and CLBC all run community events in Taipei.

items.label: Download Pleco (Chinese dictionary app)
items.description: Best Chinese dictionary app for daily vocabulary building. Useful for menus, signs, and conversations.
